AbcAdaptation.Reference.Iut.galPointMap: `galPointMap`. For fields $F$ and $\overline F$, a specified $F$-algebra structure on $\overline F$, a Weierstrass curve $E$ over $F$, and any $F$-algebra automorphism $\sigma:\overline F\to\overline F$, `galPointMap` is the additive group homomorphism from the group of nonsingular points of the base-changed curve $E_{\overline F}$ to itself which sends the point at infinity to itself and each affine point $(x,y)$ to $(\sigma(x),\sigma(y))$. The notation $\overline F$ imposes no algebraic-closure or algebraicity condition. No number-field or nonsingular-discriminant assumption is used by this definition.
AbcAdaptation.Reference.Iut.galPointMap_: `galPointMap_torsionBy`. For fields $F$ and $\overline F$, an $F$-algebra structure on $\overline F$, a Weierstrass curve $E/F$, every $F$-algebra automorphism $\sigma$ of $\overline F$, every natural number $n$, and every nonsingular point $P$ of $E_{\overline F}$ satisfying $nP=0$, the point obtained by fixing the point at infinity and applying $\sigma$ to both coordinates of affine points also satisfies $n\sigma(P)=0$. Here $n$ is not required to be prime or positive: for $n=0$ the premise includes every point, and for $n=1$ it includes only the identity. Neither a number-field assumption nor a nonsingular-discriminant assumption nor algebraic closedness of $\overline F$ is imposed.
AbcAdaptation.Reference.Iut.localComplet: `localCompletion`. For a number field $F$ with its specified field structure and a finite place $w$ of $F$, `localCompletion` is the type of the completion of $F$ for the adic valuation associated with the nonzero prime ideal of the ring of integers $\mathcal O_F$ underlying $w$. Its parameter ranges over finite places only; there is no choice of an infinite place in this definition.
AbcAdaptation.Reference.Iut.AdmissiblePr: `AdmissiblePrimeData`. Let $F$ be a number field, $E/F$ a Weierstrass curve with nonzero discriminant, $\overline F$ a field with an $F$-algebra structure, and $V$ any set of finite places of $M=\mathbb Q(j(E))\subseteq F$. No algebraic closedness or algebraicity of $\overline F/F$ is assumed. Write $G=\operatorname{Aut}_F(\overline F)$ with its Krull topology, $H=E_{\overline F}^{\mathrm{ns}}$ for the additive group of nonsingular points, $W=\{w:\text{finite place of }F\mid\exists v\in V,\;\mathfrak p_w\text{ lies over }\mathfrak p_v\}$, and $K_w$ for the $\mathfrak p_w$-adic completion of $F$. `AdmissiblePrimeData` is the type of records with precisely the following supplied components and proofs. The supplied data $D$ consist of a natural prime $\ell\ge5$; an additive group isomorphism $b:\{P\in H:\ell P=0\}\to(\mathbb Z/\ell\mathbb Z)^2$; a group homomorphism $\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb Z/\ell\mathbb Z)$ such that, for every $\sigma\in G$ and every $P$ in that torsion subgroup, $b(\sigma(P))=\rho(\sigma)b(P)$, where $\sigma$ fixes infinity and acts on both affine coordinates; the condition that each determinant-one invertible $2\times2$ matrix belongs to the image of $\rho$; openness of $\ker\rho$ in $G$; the conditions that $F/M$ is Galois and $\gcd([F:M],\ell)=1$; and, for every $v\in V$, $\gcd(\ell,\operatorname{char}(\mathcal O_M/\mathfrak p_v))=1$. In addition, for each $w\in W$ (with its membership evidence), $D$ supplies a unit $q_w\in K_w^\times$ with $\lVert q_w\rVert<1$ and an element $\pi_w\in K_w$ such that $\pi_w\ne0$, $\lVert\pi_w\rVert<1$, and for every $x\in K_w^\times$ there exists $a\in\mathbb Z$ with $\lVert x\rVert=\lVert\pi_w\rVert^a$. Put $s_r(q)=\sum_{n\ge0}(n+1)^r q^{n+1}/(1-q^{n+1})$ and let $T(q)$ be the Weierstrass curve with coefficients $(a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4,a_6)=(1,0,0,-5s_3(q),-(5s_3(q)+7s_5(q))/12)$. The further fields require $c_4(T(q_w))^3/\Delta(T(q_w))$ to equal the image of $j(E)$ under the canonical embedding $F\to K_w$; choose an integer $a_w$ satisfying $\lVert q_w\rVert=\lVert\pi_w\rVert^{a_w}$ by classical choice; and require $\gcd(\ell,\max(a_w,0))=1$, where $\max(a_w,0)$ is read as a natural number. The supplied conditions imply $a_w>0$, so this natural number is positive. The sums and field division are total operations: a nonsummable family has sum zero, and division by zero gives zero; the local ratio has no separate nonzero-discriminant field. The set $V$ may be empty, in which case all conditions indexed by $V$ or $W$ are vacuous. This is a type of data, not an assertion that such a record exists, and the fields do not require a local point-group parametrization.

AbcAdaptation.Reference.Iut.xCoord: `xCoord`. For any field $k$, a change of variables $C=(c,r,s,t)$ with $c\in k^\times$ and $r,s,t\in k$, and any Weierstrass curve $E/k$, `xCoord` is the function from the group of nonsingular points of $E$ to $k$ which assigns zero to the point at infinity and assigns $(x-r)/c^2$ to an affine point $(x,y)$. The curve is an implicit argument and need not have nonzero discriminant; the denominator is nonzero because $c$ is a unit. The value at infinity is the explicitly assigned field element zero, not a projective affine coordinate. Valuation, rank-one, and completeness hypotheses from the surrounding section are unused in this definition.
AbcAdaptation.Reference.Iut.yCoord: `yCoord`. For any field $k$, a change of variables $C=(c,r,s,t)$ with $c\in k^\times$ and $r,s,t\in k$, and any Weierstrass curve $E/k$, `yCoord` is the function from the group of nonsingular points of $E$ to $k$ which assigns zero to the point at infinity and assigns $(y-t-s(x-r))/c^3$ to an affine point $(x,y)$. The curve is an implicit argument and need not have nonzero discriminant; the denominator is nonzero because $c$ is a unit. The value at infinity is the explicitly assigned field element zero. Valuation, rank-one, and completeness hypotheses from the surrounding section are unused in this definition.
AbcAdaptation.Reference.Iut.TateStructur: `TateStructure`. Let $k$ be a field with a specified valuation $v:k\to\{0\}\cup\{\text{multiplicatively written integers}\}$, a rank-one structure on $v$, and the resulting normed-field structure, and let $E/k$ be a Weierstrass curve. The valuation codomain is the ordered group $(\mathbb Z,+)$ written multiplicatively with an absorbing zero adjoined, not the usual nonnegative integers. No nonzero-discriminant condition on $E$ is stipulated. `TateStructure` is the type of records with the following supplied data and proofs. A record $S$ supplies a unit $q\in k^\times$ with $\lVert q\rVert<1$; a change of variables $C=(c,r,s,t)$ with $c\in k^\times$ and $r,s,t\in k$; an equality $C\cdot E=T(q)$; and an additive group isomorphism $\phi:(k^\times/\langle q\rangle)_{\mathrm{add}}\to E^{\mathrm{ns}}(k)$, where $\langle q\rangle=\{q^n:n\in\mathbb Z\}$, the quotient is by this subgroup, and its multiplication is written as addition in the source of $\phi$. Here $s_j(q)=\sum_{n\ge0}(n+1)^j q^{n+1}/(1-q^{n+1})$ and $T(q)$ has Weierstrass coefficients $(1,0,0,-5s_3(q),-(5s_3(q)+7s_5(q))/12)$. The equality uses the change $x=c^2X+r$, $y=c^3Y+c^2sX+t$. Define $X_q(u)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}q^nu/(1-q^nu)^2-2s_1(q)$ and $Y_q(u)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}(q^nu)^2/(1-q^nu)^3+s_1(q)$ for $u\in k^\times$. For every such $u$ satisfying $q^nu\ne1$ for every $n\in\mathbb Z$, the record requires the transformed coordinates of $\phi([u])$ to equal $X_q(u)$ and $Y_q(u)$ respectively; the transformed coordinates of an affine point $(x,y)$ are $(x-r)/c^2$ and $(y-t-s(x-r))/c^3$, and both are defined to be zero at infinity. There is no coordinate-equality requirement for units failing that universal condition. All sums and divisions are totalized, with nonsummable sums equal to zero and division by zero equal to zero; in particular this convention also applies to the coefficient divided by $12$ in characteristics $2$ and $3$. Completeness of $k$ is not an assumption of this declaration. Existence of a record is not asserted.

`TateStructure.IsCanonical`. Let $k$ be a field with a specified valuation $v:k\to\{0\}\cup\{\text{multiplicatively written integers}\}$, a rank-one structure on $v$, and the resulting normed-field structure, and let $E/k$ be a Weierstrass curve. The valuation codomain is the ordered group $(\mathbb Z,+)$ written multiplicatively with an absorbing zero adjoined, not the usual nonnegative integers. No nonzero-discriminant condition on $E$ is stipulated. A record $S$ supplies a unit $q\in k^\times$ with $\lVert q\rVert<1$; a change of variables $C=(c,r,s,t)$ with $c\in k^\times$ and $r,s,t\in k$; an equality $C\cdot E=T(q)$; and an additive group isomorphism $\phi:(k^\times/\langle q\rangle)_{\mathrm{add}}\to E^{\mathrm{ns}}(k)$, where $\langle q\rangle=\{q^n:n\in\mathbb Z\}$, the quotient is by this subgroup, and its multiplication is written as addition in the source of $\phi$. Here $s_j(q)=\sum_{n\ge0}(n+1)^j q^{n+1}/(1-q^{n+1})$ and $T(q)$ has Weierstrass coefficients $(1,0,0,-5s_3(q),-(5s_3(q)+7s_5(q))/12)$. The equality uses the change $x=c^2X+r$, $y=c^3Y+c^2sX+t$. Define $X_q(u)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}q^nu/(1-q^nu)^2-2s_1(q)$ and $Y_q(u)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}(q^nu)^2/(1-q^nu)^3+s_1(q)$ for $u\in k^\times$. For every such $u$ satisfying $q^nu\ne1$ for every $n\in\mathbb Z$, the record requires the transformed coordinates of $\phi([u])$ to equal $X_q(u)$ and $Y_q(u)$ respectively; the transformed coordinates of an affine point $(x,y)$ are $(x-r)/c^2$ and $(y-t-s(x-r))/c^3$, and both are defined to be zero at infinity. There is no coordinate-equality requirement for units failing that universal condition. All sums and divisions are totalized, with nonsummable sums equal to zero and division by zero equal to zero; in particular this convention also applies to the coefficient divided by $12$ in characteristics $2$ and $3$. Completeness of $k$ is not an assumption of this declaration. For every such specified $S$, every natural number $\ell$, and every nonsingular point $P\in E^{\mathrm{ns}}(k)$, `IsCanonical` is the proposition that there exist a unit $u\in k^\times$ with $\phi([u])=P$ and an integer $m$ such that $u^\ell=q^{1+\ell m}$ or $u^\ell=q^{-1+\ell m}$, with these equations taken in the unit group and the exponents on $q$ taken in $\mathbb Z$. Thus one unit and one integer are chosen before the disjunction. No primality or positivity assumption on $\ell$ is present. For $\ell=0$ the equations reduce to $1=q$ or $1=q^{-1}$, which cannot hold because $\lVert q\rVert<1$, so no point has this property. For $\ell=1$ the equations make $u$ a power of $q$, so the property holds exactly for the zero point.
